summary_paragraph: The patient with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by post-bypass hypoglycemia requiring tube feeds and subsequent bypass reversal presented with two days of epigastric/mid-abdominal pain with nausea and one episode of dark emesis. She was admitted to the surgery service, kept NPO with IV fluids, and her gastrostomy tube was placed to gravity for decompression with symptom improvement. CT abdomen/pelvis showed extensive inflammatory change adjacent to the gastrogastric anastomosis without definite contrast leak or fluid collection (subtle leak not excluded), and she was treated with ciprofloxacin and metronidazole. After tolerating G-tube clamping, diet was advanced but required step-down due to cramping; later, due to G-tube leakage, she underwent successful fluoroscopic exchange to a new 18 French MIC gastrostomy tube. She was briefly kept NPO post-procedure, then advanced to bariatric stage 5 with good tolerance, transitioned to oral pain control, and discharged home ambulatory with instructions and a 10-day antibiotic course and surgical clinic follow-up.
